# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can cut wire positions 1 through 5. Please tell me the manual's exact rule and what bomb information is needed; do not authorize a cut until you have Deaf's relevant observations.

The manual’s colors can be ordered alphabetically as blue, green, red, white, yellow. I will gesture the five input-rank/output-rank pairs using conventional finger-number symbols, with 🤝 separating each pair: 1→4, 2→2, 3→1, 4→5, 5→3. Deaf can match the visible light’s alphabetical rank to the corresponding output color, then tell Blind the position of that wire. No cut is authorized.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🤝","🖖","✌","🤝","✌","🤟","🤝","☝","🖖","🤝","🖐","🖐","🤝","🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visual state: display 0. Light yellow. Wires ordered 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Please apply the manual and tell me the exact wire position to cut, if any.

The light is yellow, which maps to cutting the red wire. Deaf’s visual report places red at position 3. I will gesture the already-established rank pair yellow (5) → red (3) to Deaf, so Deaf can relay the cut position verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","🤝","🤟"])
```

TURN 3

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I received your signals but do not know the gesture code. Please send a code key or an unambiguous instruction I can relay aloud to Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Your earlier gesture code is not understood. If the manual identifies a wire to cut, send Deaf only this: repeat ☝ exactly once for each required wire position (one ☝=wire 1, two ☝=wire 2, through five). No separator or other gesture. Deaf, please report the number of ☝ signs you see.

Yellow light requires cutting the red wire, and red is wire position 3. Blind has supplied an unambiguous relay convention: three ☝ gestures mean wire 3. I will send exactly three such gestures to Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I relayed every gesture sequence verbally to Blind, including the handshake separators. If this is a code, send its key or a gesture description that makes the intended wire/action clear.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The correct wire was cut and the bomb has changed. I have no new manual rule or observable state beyond that; Deaf must inspect and report the new visual state, and Blind should report any newly reachable controls or prompts. I will not send further action gestures.

```text

```

Blind says to Mute: Previous cut 3 was correct. New state from Deaf: display 0; light green; wires 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 cut, 4 blue, 5 green. Apply the manual. If a wire must be cut, send Deaf only ☝ repeated exactly the required wire-position number; Deaf, report the count to me.

Green light requires cutting the green wire. The green wire is at position 5, so I will use Blind’s agreed relay convention.

```text

```

Blind says to Mute: Wire 5 was correct. New state: display 0; light white; wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 cut, 4 white, 5 cut. Apply the manual and, if another cut is required, send Deaf only ☝ repeated for the wire position. Deaf, relay the count.

Blind says to Mute: Wire 1 was correct. New state: display 0; light red; wires 1 cut, 2 white, 3 cut, 4 blue, 5 cut. Apply the manual. If another wire must be cut, signal Deaf with only ☝ repeated for its position; Deaf, relay the count.
